description: We are building an interactive web application to map and visualize Earth analogs for Moon and Mars bases. I am a full-stack developer (React/Node.js) looking for passionate team members to join forces. If you have skills or interests in Earth Science, Data Analysis, Data Visualization, or UI/UX Design to help process NASA datasets and create an amazing tool, join us! Let's build something out of this world.
summary: AstroAnalogs is an interactive planetary-analog screening platform built with Laravel Blade, JavaScript, Three.js and Chart.js. It helps researchers compare selected terrestrial environments with lunar and Martian target regions. The application provides a 3D Earth locator, a curated database of volcanic, subsurface, arid and extreme-environment sites, side-by-side visual comparisons, similarity charts, and a scientific report highlighting differences in gravity, radiation and atmospheric pressure. Its Auto Discover and Custom Scan workflows rank a curated set of candidates using weighted geology, topography, temperature, slope and mineral-preference criteria. NASA POWER climatology enriches temperature comparisons, while NASA GIBS supplies Earth-observation map imagery and NASA CMR provides searchable collection and granule metadata. By showing both potential matches and important limitations, AstroAnalogs supports transparent early-stage analog screening and helps identify terrestrial environments for testing planetary exploration technologies. Scores are screening rankings, not validated predictions.
details:
AstroAnalogs is an interactive, data-driven planetary analog discovery and comparison platform developed to help researchers identify terrestrial environments that can support future Moon and Mars exploration. Rather than focusing on a single location, our project brings together a curated global collection of unusual geological and environmental sites within one integrated research system.

How It Works

The platform consists of several interconnected modules. Mission Control provides an interactive 3D Earth globe with terrestrial analog location markers and mission information. The Terrestrial Database organizes research locations into subsurface lava tubes, extreme biological environments, and arid and volcanic terrains. Planetary Targets provides lunar and Martian reference locations. Users can select an Earth analog and a planetary target to explore their characteristics through side-by-side imagery, quantitative similarity charts, and scientific limitation reports.

Our AI Matchmaker introduces two discovery workflows. Auto Discover ranks curated research candidates using geology (40%), topography (30%), and environmental similarity (30%), enriched with NASA POWER climate data when available. Custom Scan allows users to specify preferred temperature, terrain slope, mineral family, and target mission, then generates an explainable ranking of suitable candidates. The scoring engine is deterministic rather than a trained machine-learning model, making its results transparent and reproducible.

NASA Data Integration

We integrate NASA POWER climatology, NASA GIBS Earth-observation imagery, NASA CMR collection and granule metadata, and the NASA Mars Rover Photos API. These resources support environmental comparisons, Earth imagery exploration, and access to planetary research information.

Technology Stack and Development Tools

The backend is developed using PHP and the Laravel framework, with Laravel Blade for server-rendered application pages. The frontend is built using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. We use Tailwind CSS for interface styling and Font Awesome for icons. Three.js and WebGL power interactive 3D planetary visualizations, while Chart.js generates quantitative similarity charts and scientific data visualizations. MathJax renders mathematical equations in scientific documentation. The application also uses browser-based JavaScript API requests and local storage for client-side functionality. Development and testing were carried out using Visual Studio Code and a web browser. No specialized hardware is required.

Innovation, Benefits and Intended Impact

Our key innovation is combining candidate discovery, multi-criteria comparison, scientific transparency, and mission-oriented applications in one accessible platform. We deliberately highlight where analogies break down, including differences in gravity, radiation, and atmospheric pressure, instead of claiming that any Earth location is an exact planetary equivalent.

The intended impact is to help researchers and future mission designers prioritize promising field-testing environments for rover mobility, instrument calibration, subsurface exploration, resource investigation, and astrobiology research. AstroAnalogs aims to make planetary analog research more systematic, accessible, explainable, and useful for future space exploration.
